verification_methodology_note:
PRIMARY-TIER GAP: laws.boe.gov.sa (Bureau of Experts, the definitive first-party Saudi government legal portal) was attempted directly during this build pass at the specific LawDetails URL located via web search (https://laws.boe.gov.sa/BoeLaws/Laws/LawDetails/85eb2897-bec6-4c0c-b1d7-ac7c008ec09c/1) and returned HTTP 503 Service Unavailable; a second BOE SearchDetails URL variant also returned HTTP 503. This matches the prior research pass's finding (direct fetch: HTTP 503 / connection failure; r.jina.ai proxy: 15s navigation timeout) and this corpus's established BOE-egress-blocked pattern for other tracks. Not bypassed via any hostname trick, per corpus policy. web.archive.org was likewise confirmed unreachable in the prior pass (403 AbuseAlleviationError) and was not retried.

SECONDARY-TIER SOURCES (this track's actual basis): (1) nezams.com — consolidated text with inline amendment notes; (2) mustsharik.com — consolidated text with chapter headings and amendment notes, updated to reflect amendments through 1442H; (3) mohamah.net — original pre-amendment 1429H text with full chapter headings (missing Article 15 — see known_unresolved_discrepancies). All 30 articles were transcribed from the prior research pass's consolidated file (scratchpad/anti_commercial_fraud_law_consolidated.md), which itself triangulated these three sources article-by-article. During THIS build pass, a fresh independent WebFetch of both nezams.com (https://nezams.com/نظام-مكافحة-الغش-التجاري/) and mustsharik.com (https://mustsharik.com/leg65/) was performed and cross-checked against a sample of five articles (1, 5, 13, 23, 25) plus their amendment citations; all five matched the consolidated file's transcription verbatim, including the exact wording of Article 13's pre- and post-amendment text and Article 23's two-paragraph post-amendment restructuring. No discrepancy was found in this sample re-check beyond what the prior pass had already flagged.

ARTICLE 5 SECOND-AMENDMENT CITATION (adding وزارة الصحة) — ADDITIONAL VERIFICATION ATTEMPTED THIS PASS: the prior pass left this disputed between nezams.com's 'قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (508) وتاريخ 1442/9/1هـ' and mustsharik.com's 'المرسوم الملكي رقم (م/76) وتاريخ 1442/9/3هـ'. This pass located, via web search, an Umm al-Qura official-gazette URL whose own indexed title reads 'تعديل المادة (الخامسة) من نظام مكافحة الغش التجاري' (https://uqn.gov.sa/تعديل-المادة-الخامسة-من-نظام-مكافحة-ال/) — a first-party gazette notice specifically about this amendment — but a direct WebFetch of that URL returned HTTP 404 (the page is genuinely dead/removed, consistent with this law's Article 23 gazette URL already being confirmed dead in the prior pass). A WebSearch aggregation of that same dead URL's search-engine-indexed snippet independently states 'Council of Ministers Resolution No. 508 dated 01/09/1442 AH... published in Umm Al-Qura' as the amending instrument. Separately, a genuine news article (alwatan.com, https://www.alwatan.com.sa/article/1074373, on adding health inspectors to the anti-fraud enforcement system) was fetched directly and quotes the instrument type verbatim as 'صدر قرار مجلس الوزراء القاضي بتعديل المادة الخامسة...' (a Council of Ministers decision) without giving its number — corroborating the INSTRUMENT TYPE nezams.com and the indexed gazette snippet both claim (قرار مجلس الوزراء), not mustsharik.com's Royal Decree claim. This shifts the weight of evidence toward Council of Ministers Resolution No. 508 (1/9/1442H) being the more likely correct citation, but it remains NOT first-party-confirmed this pass (the one gazette URL specifically about this amendment returned 404 on direct fetch, and BOE itself returned 503) — both candidate citations are therefore still recorded in Article 5's history entry rather than silently picking one, consistent with this corpus's established convention for genuinely disputed citations (cf. income_tax_law Article 66's dual-dated M/52 conflict).

ARTICLE 5 CURRENT-TEXT RECONSTRUCTION: no single source found (this pass or the prior pass) presents Article 5's fully consolidated post-both-amendments text as one verbatim block — nezams.com and mustsharik.com both display the ORIGINAL 1429H sentence in the article body, with the two amendments described only as separate prose notes ('عُدلت هذه المادة ... بإضافة عبارة ...'). This track's 'text' field for Article 5 is therefore a mechanical splice: the verbatim original sentence (itself confirmed identical across nezams.com, mustsharik.com, and mohamah.net) with the two verbatim-quoted inserted phrases ('ووزارة الطاقة والصناعة والثروة المعدنية' and 'وزارة الصحة') placed at the positions both sources' amendment notes describe. The exact final ordering/punctuation of the fully consolidated sentence has not been independently confirmed against a single primary-source rendering (BOE remains unreachable) — flagged transparently in known_unresolved_discrepancies rather than presented as directly-sourced verbatim.

ORIGINAL (1429H) PRE-AMENDMENT TEXT: populated for all 5 amended articles (5, 13, 23, 25, 27) — each original sentence is explicitly given, verbatim, in the consolidated research file (sourced from mohamah.net's 2017 pre-amendment transcription for Article 5, and from nezams.com's own before/after amendment-note presentation for Articles 13, 23, 25, and 27) — none fabricated or reconstructed.

No legal text is altered, paraphrased, summarized, or machine-translated in this track. Arabic governs; no English or Chinese text is produced.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: Article 5's SECOND amendment (adding وزارة الصحة / Ministry of Health) carries a genuinely disputed citation between secondary sources: nezams.com states "قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (508) وتاريخ 1442/9/1هـ" (a Council of Ministers Resolution); mustsharik.com and two independent WebSearch AI-aggregations state "المرسوم الملكي رقم (م/76) وتاريخ 1442/9/3هـ" (a Royal Decree). This build pass attempted one further direct resolution: a web search located an Umm al-Qura official-gazette URL whose own indexed page title is literally "تعديل المادة (الخامسة) من نظام مكافحة الغش التجاري" (https://uqn.gov.sa/تعديل-المادة-الخامسة-من-نظام-مكافحة-ال/) -- but a direct WebFetch of that URL returned HTTP 404 (dead link, consistent with this law's Article 23 gazette URL already being confirmed dead in the prior research pass). A WebSearch aggregation of that same URL's indexed snippet states the amending instrument as 'Council of Ministers Resolution No. 508 dated 01/09/1442 AH published in Umm Al-Qura'. Separately, a genuine news article (alwatan.com/article/1074373, on adding health inspectors to the enforcement system) was fetched directly and quotes the instrument TYPE verbatim as a Council of Ministers decision ('صدر قرار مجلس الوزراء القاضي بتعديل المادة الخامسة...'), without a number. laws.boe.gov.sa itself returned HTTP 503 on direct fetch this pass (twice, at two different URL forms), confirming it is genuinely unreachable, not bypassed. Net effect: this pass's additional evidence shifts the balance toward Council of Ministers Resolution No. 508 (1/9/1442H) being the more likely correct instrument TYPE, but it is still NOT first-party-confirmed (the one gazette page specifically about this amendment is dead). BOTH candidate citations are recorded in Article 5's history entry rather than silently picking one, matching this corpus's established convention for genuinely disputed citations (cf. income_tax_law Article 66's dual-dated M/52 conflict).

No single source (this pass or the prior research pass) presents Article 5's fully consolidated post-both-amendments text as one verbatim block: nezams.com and mustsharik.com both display the ORIGINAL 1429H sentence in the article body, with the two amendments described only as separate prose amendment-notes. This track's current 'text' field for Article 5 is a mechanical splice of the verbatim original sentence (confirmed identical across nezams.com, mustsharik.com, and mohamah.net) with the two verbatim-quoted inserted phrases ('ووزارة الطاقة والصناعة والثروة المعدنية' and 'وزارة الصحة') placed at the positions both sources' amendment notes describe. The precise final punctuation/ordering of the fully consolidated sentence has not been independently confirmed against a single primary-source rendering, since BOE remains unreachable -- flagged transparently here rather than presented as directly-sourced verbatim from one document.

mohamah.net's 2017 transcription of this law is missing Article 15 (المادة الخامسة عشرة) entirely -- confirmed via grep, no occurrence of "الخامسة عشرة" anywhere on that page. Article 15 is present, word-for-word identical, in both nezams.com and mustsharik.com. Treated as a mohamah.net transcription/scraping error, not a genuine textual variant; Article 15's text in this track rests on nezams.com/mustsharik.com.

Article 1's definitions of "الوزارة" (وزارة التجارة والصناعة) and "الوزير" (وزير التجارة والصناعة), and Article 4's reference to "الوزارة", still name the combined Ministry of Commerce AND Industry -- an entity later reorganized/split into separate Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Industry & Mineral Resources bodies at various points since 2008. No source found identifies a formal textual amendment updating this definitional reference. Preserved verbatim as a likely-stale-but-not-formally-amended reference, not modernized.

Article 12 still names "هيئة التحقيق والادعاء العام" as the body with investigation/prosecution jurisdiction, even though this body was itself renamed/restructured into "النيابة العامة" (Public Prosecution) government-wide by Royal Order in 1439H/2017 -- the same reorganization explicitly reflected in Article 23's own 1442H amendment (which replaced "هيئة التحقيق والادعاء العام" with "النيابة العامة"). No source found reports Article 12 itself as formally amended. Flagged as possible additional unflagged staleness, not treated as a confirmed amendment absent a primary source that says so.

The fine amounts in Articles 16-20 (up to 500,000 SAR / 50,000 SAR / 1,000,000 SAR) show no confirmed increase since this law's original 1429H (2008) enactment in any source consulted across either research pass. This is documented as a confirmed-unchanged finding, not an assumption that periodic fine increases have or have not occurred.

A draft "Comprehensive Consumer Protection Law" (نظام حماية المستهلك) was put out for public consultation in March-May 2022 via the Istitlaa platform, but remains UNENACTED as of this build (2026-07-18): a direct site-search of laws.boe.gov.sa for "حماية المستهلك" returns no such comprehensive law (only the narrower "تنظيم جمعية حماية المستهلك", a Consumer Protection SOCIETY/NGO regulation), the Ministry of Commerce's own consumer-protection materials still frame consumer protection as arising from this Anti-Commercial Fraud Law plus the separate E-Commerce Law, and no 2023-2026 news reports the draft's passage. This Anti-Commercial Fraud Law (M/19, 1429H) is confirmed as the correct, currently-binding build target. Forward-looking flag: a future superseding comprehensive consumer-protection statute may be enacted after this build date.

A companion Implementing Regulation (اللائحة التنفيذية لنظام مكافحة الغش التجاري) exists, issued via Ministerial Resolution No. 155 dated 6/1/1431H (per nezams.com's "الملحقات" field, independently corroborated by justice-square.com's reference to "لائحة نظام الغش التجاري الصادرة في 1431/01/06هـ"). Per task scope, its text is NOT extracted in this track -- only its existence/citation is noted here, consistent with how other tracks in this corpus handle unextracted companion instruments.

laws.boe.gov.sa was retried directly during this build pass at the specific LawDetails URL for this law located via web search (https://laws.boe.gov.sa/BoeLaws/Laws/LawDetails/85eb2897-bec6-4c0c-b1d7-ac7c008ec09c/1) and at a SearchDetails URL variant; both returned HTTP 503 Service Unavailable, confirming the portal is genuinely unreachable from this environment this pass, matching this corpus's established BOE-egress-blocked pattern for other tracks. Not bypassed via any hostname trick, per policy.

Two distinct Umm al-Qura official-gazette URLs relevant to this law's amendment history were located via web search this pass but both returned HTTP 404 on direct fetch: the Article 5 second-amendment notice (uqn.gov.sa/تعديل-المادة-الخامسة-من-نظام-مكافحة-ال/) and the Article 23 amendment-approval notice (uqn.gov.sa/الموافقة-على-تعديل-المادة-الثالثة-وال/, already noted dead in the prior research pass under its old ?p=6907 URL form). Both are genuinely dead/redirected links (the site appears to have been redesigned), not an egress block; their content is only available via secondary corroboration (search-engine-indexed snippets and independent secondary sources), not first-party confirmed.

Council of Ministers Decision No. (107) dated 19/3/1435H empowers the Minister of Commerce and Industry to designate SASO (Saudi Standards, Metrology and Quality Organization) staff as judicial officers (مأمورو ضبط قضائي) for violations of this law -- an implementing/enabling decision under Article 5, NOT a textual amendment to any article. Single-sourced (nezams.com only) and not independently cross-verified this pass. Noted as a candidate companion record, not treated as an article amendment.

The prior research pass's consolidated markdown file states in its own narrative summary (twice) that "24 of 30 articles remain أصلية (original/unamended)". Recounting that same file's own per-article STATUS tags during this build pass found exactly 5 articles marked معدلة (5, 13, 23, 25, 27) and 25 marked أصلية -- i.e. the research file's own narrative summary undercounted أصلية articles by one relative to its own per-article tagging. This track's status_counts (25 اصلية / 5 معدلة / 0 ملغاة / 0 مضافة) reflects the corrected per-article recount, not the research file's narrative summary figure.

**تنبيه سريان**: النسخة المُستوعبة هنا منشورة بتاريخ 2008-04-30، وقد رصد تدقيق السريان (scripts/audit_corpus_currency.py) إشعاري تعديل في أرشيف جريدة أم القرى **بعد** هذا التاريخ، يحمل عنوانه اسم هذه الأداة بكل كلماته المميِّزة ونوعها ذاته (نظام): 2021-08-13 — الموافقة على تعديل المادة (الثالثة والعشرين) من نظام مكافحة الغش التجاري (https://www.uqn.gov.sa/details?p=18118)؛ 2021-04-30 — تعديل المادة (الخامسة) من نظام مكافحة الغش التجاري (https://www.uqn.gov.sa/details?p=17536). **الإشعار ليس نص التعديل**، ولذلك لا يُدَّعى هنا شيء عن مضمونه ولم يُعدَّل نص أي مادة استناداً إليه. والمطابقة على العنوان لا على المتن، وقد يَرِد اسم أداة داخل عنوانٍ موضوعُه أداة مجاورة، فالصفحة الرسمية المذكورة هي الفيصل. المُفصَح عنه هو أن نص هذا المسار **قد لا يكون محدَّثاً**. يُرفع هذا التنبيه فقط عند استيعاب النص المعدَّل من مصدر رسمي. (تاريخ الطبعة أعلاه محسوب من التاريخ الهجري المُثبَت في المصدر، لا مقروءاً من ترويسة الجريدة؛ وقد اشتُرط فارق ثلاثين يوماً على الأقل حتى لا يُنتج خطأ التحويل تنبيهاً كاذباً.)
